comment: The supported extensions: what the Manage Extensions window offers, and the policy each
one is held to. It ships inside the app and is not user-editable. Anything not listed can
still be installed from the window's footer, behind a warning, as an unsupported extension.
Two kinds of entry, by where the extension comes from:
webstore  `id` set. Installs and updates to the NEWEST store release. The CRX signature
must prove this id; there is deliberately no byte pin (decided 2026-09-24).
archive   `archive` set: a GitHub repo pinned to one reviewed commit. An unpacked build
is unsigned, so it is pinned by the hash of its files (see allowlist.js
hashTree). `treeSha256` lists every build still accepted at load, so an app
update that moves the pin does not unload the build a user already has;
`archive.treeSha256` is the one offered for install.
`source` is the page the window links to. `minVersion` is a floor.
permissions, optionalPermissions, hostPermissions and contentScriptMatches are the
maximum the manifest may ask for. A build asking for anything else is refused, and an
update that does so leaves the installed version in place. Optional permissions are listed
only so they can be recognised: ShapeShell always refuses chrome.permissions.request.

extensions.name: Bitwarden Password Manager
extensions.reviewed: 2026-09-20, version 2026.8.0; tracks the newest store release since 2026-09-24
extensions.notes: Broad host access is inherent to a password manager: it fills forms on any site, and Onshape sign-in passes through other hosts. Verified working in ShapeShell: login, 2FA, unlock and autofill.

extensions.name: Onshape Drawing Comfort
extensions.notes: GitHub only and 0BSD licensed, so it has no key and no stable extension id; it is pinned by the hash of its files, and installed from GitHub's archive of the reviewed commit (verified 2026-09-24 to hash identically to a clone). Dark-mode palettes for the drawing editor. Storage only, and scoped to onshape.com.
